title: Make addition behave like a value
prompt: Money stores cents. Adding two amounts returns a new Money whose cents equal the sum. Neither operand changes. All tested sums fit in int. Equality compares cents.
signature: class Money: friend Money operator+(Money,Money); int cents() const
starter:
#include <iostream>

class Money{int cents_;public:explicit Money(int n):cents_(n){}int cents()const{return cents_;}friend Money operator+(Money a,Money b){return Money(a.cents_-b.cents_);}friend bool operator==(Money a,Money b){return a.cents_==b.cents_;}};
solution:
#include <iostream>

class Money{int cents_;public:explicit Money(int n):cents_(n){}int cents()const{return cents_;}friend Money operator+(Money a,Money b){return Money(a.cents_+b.cents_);}friend bool operator==(Money a,Money b){return a.cents_==b.cents_;}};

tests.label: Two positive
tests.hint: Use addition for the new amount.

hints: The + operator can be defined for a class if its meaning is clear.
Return a new Money value rather than changing either input.
explanation: The operator is a function called by a+b. Here friend gives it access to the private stored cents; pass-by-value keeps the operands independent.
chapterTitle: Designing Natural Types with Operator Overloading
